source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Exact source records mapped to established public labels; mapping is recorded for every verse and verified against source KJV annotations. Daniel, Hosea, Joel, Jonah, Micah, and Nahum have chapter-boundary differences.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps the brief attribution without adding a reign or date absent from the source.
verses.before: The word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel.
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Joel son of Pethuel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel.

verses.rationale: Retains the two audiences and the unprecedented-event question.
verses.before: Hear this, elders, and give ear, all inhabitants of the land. Has anything like this happened in your days, or in the days of your ancestors?
verses.after: Hear this, elders! Listen, everyone living in the land! Has anything like this happened in your days or in the days of your ancestors?
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear this, elders, and give ear, all inhabitants of the land. Has anything like this happened in your days, or in the days of your ancestors?

verses.rationale: Preserves the four-generation transmission instead of shortening it to a general remembrance.
verses.before: Tell it to your children, and let your children tell their children, and their children another generation.
verses.after: Tell your children about it; let your children tell their children, and their children the generation after them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Tell it to your children, and let your children tell their children, and their children another generation.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four Hebrew locust terms and the three repeated consumption clauses; labels are descriptive, not a biological claim.
verses.before: What the cutting locust left, the swarming locust ate; what the swarming locust left, the hopping locust ate; and what the hopping locust left, the destroying locust ate.
verses.after: What the cutting locust left, the swarming locust ate. What the swarming locust left, the creeping locust ate. What the creeping locust left, the stripping locust ate.
verses.tsw_comparator: What the cutting locust left, the swarming locust ate; what the swarming locust left, the hopping locust ate; and what the hopping locust left, the destroying locust ate.

verses.rationale: Retains the specific addressees and the mouth image rather than generic economic loss.
verses.before: Wake up, you who are drunk, and weep; wail, all you who drink wine, over the sweet wine, for it is cut off from your mouth.
verses.after: Wake up, drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you wine drinkers, for the sweet wine has been cut off from your mouths.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wake up, you who are drunk, and weep; wail, all you who drink wine, over the sweet wine, for it is cut off from your mouth.

verses.rationale: Preserves nation and predatory teeth while leaving the locust/army imagery intertwined.
verses.before: For a nation has come up against my land, mighty and without number. Its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and it has the fangs of a lioness.
verses.after: A nation has come up against my land, powerful and beyond counting. Its teeth are a lion’s teeth; it has the fangs of a lioness.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a nation has come up against my land, mighty and without number. Its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and it has the fangs of a lioness.

verses.rationale: Keeps the possessive landowner voice and the visible whiteness of stripped branches.
verses.before: It has made my vine a desolation and my fig tree a splintered thing. It has stripped it bare and thrown it down; its branches have become white.
verses.after: It has devastated my vine and stripped my fig tree bare. It has peeled it completely and thrown it aside; its branches have turned white.
verses.tsw_comparator: It has made my vine a desolation and my fig tree a splintered thing. It has stripped it bare and thrown it down; its branches have become white.

verses.rationale: Retains the bereaved young woman and husband relationship, with betrothed possibility in notes.
verses.before: Lament like a young woman wearing sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
verses.after: Lament like a young woman clothed in sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lament like a young woman wearing sackcloth for the husband of her youth.

verses.rationale: Preserves both offerings and both divine-name occurrences.
verses.before: Grain offering and drink offering are cut off from the house of the LORD. The priests mourn, the servants of the LORD.
verses.after: Grain offering and drink offering have been cut off from the house of the LORD. The priests mourn, those who serve the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Grain offering and drink offering are cut off from the house of the LORD. The priests mourn, the servants of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the personified ground and repeated devastation before the three produce losses.
verses.before: The field is devastated; the ground mourns, for the grain is devastated, the new wine has dried up, and the oil languishes.
verses.after: The fields are devastated; the ground mourns. Grain is devastated, new wine has dried up, and oil has failed.
verses.tsw_comparator: The field is devastated; the ground mourns, for the grain is devastated, the new wine has dried up, and the oil languishes.

verses.rationale: Preserves shame/drying wordplay as shame here and keeps both crops.
verses.before: Be ashamed, farmers; wail, vineyard workers, over the wheat and over the barley, for the harvest of the field has perished.
verses.after: Be ashamed, farmers! Wail, vine growers, for the wheat and barley, because the harvest of the fields is lost.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be ashamed, farmers; wail, vineyard workers, over the wheat and over the barley, for the harvest of the field has perished.

verses.rationale: Retains the full tree list and repeated drying that culminates in human joy.
verses.before: The vine has dried up, and the fig tree languishes. Pomegranate, palm, and apple tree— all the trees of the field have dried up. Indeed, joy has dried up from humanity.
verses.after: The vine has dried up; the fig tree has withered. Pomegranate, palm, and apple— all the trees of the field have dried up. Joy itself has dried up among human beings.
verses.tsw_comparator: The vine has dried up, and the fig tree languishes. Pomegranate, palm, and apple tree— all the trees of the field have dried up. Indeed, joy has dried up from humanity.

verses.rationale: Keeps nightlong mourning and the my/your God shift.
verses.before: Put on sackcloth and lament, priests; wail, servants of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, servants of my God, for grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.
verses.after: Put on sackcloth and lament, priests! Wail, you who serve at the altar! Come, spend the night in sackcloth, you who serve my God, for grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Put on sackcloth and lament, priests; wail, servants of the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, servants of my God, for grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the coordinated communal actions and twice-named recipient.
verses.before: Consecrate a fast; call a solemn assembly. Gather the elders, all the inhabitants of the land, to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
verses.after: Set apart a fast; call a solemn assembly. Gather the elders and everyone living in the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Consecrate a fast; call a solemn assembly. Gather the elders, all the inhabitants of the land, to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the shod/Shaddai connection through devastation/Almighty explained in the note.
verses.before: Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is near; it will come like destruction from the Almighty.
verses.after: Alas for the day! The day of the LORD is near; it comes like devastation from the Almighty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is near; it will come like destruction from the Almighty.

verses.rationale: Maintains the rhetorical question and parallel loss of food and worship's joy.
verses.before: Is not food cut off before our eyes, joy and gladness from the house of our God?
verses.after: Has not food been cut off before our eyes, and joy and celebration from the house of our God?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not food cut off before our eyes, joy and gladness from the house of our God?

verses.rationale: Chooses the common contextual sense of three rare opening words while explicitly flagging their uncertainty.
verses.before: The seeds shrivel under their clods. The storehouses are desolate; the granaries are torn down, for the grain has dried up.
verses.after: Seeds shrivel beneath the clods. Storehouses stand deserted; granaries are torn down, for the grain has dried up.
verses.tsw_comparator: The seeds shrivel under their clods. The storehouses are desolate; the granaries are torn down, for the grain has dried up.

verses.rationale: Preserves cattle and sheep and their suffering without attributing moral guilt to the animals.
verses.before: How the animals groan! The herds of cattle wander in confusion because there is no pasture for them; even the flocks of sheep suffer.
verses.after: How the animals groan! Herds of cattle wander in distress because they have no pasture. Even the flocks of sheep suffer.
verses.tsw_comparator: How the animals groan! The herds of cattle wander in confusion because there is no pasture for them; even the flocks of sheep suffer.

verses.rationale: Keeps the first-person prayer and parallel fire/flame devastation.
verses.before: To you, O LORD, I call, for fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness, and flame has burned all the trees of the field.
verses.after: To you, LORD, I cry, for fire has consumed the wilderness pastures and flame has burned all the trees of the field.
verses.tsw_comparator: To you, O LORD, I call, for fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness, and flame has burned all the trees of the field.

verses.rationale: Preserves animal appeal to God and the repeated pasture clause.
verses.before: Even the animals of the field long for you, for the channels of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness.
verses.after: Even the wild animals pant toward you, for the streambeds have dried up and fire has consumed the wilderness pastures.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even the animals of the field long for you, for the channels of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the pastures of the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Retains abrupt divine my within the call and repeats the near-day announcement.
verses.before: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion; sound the alarm on my holy mountain. Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of the LORD is coming; indeed, it is near—
verses.after: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion! Sound the alarm on my holy mountain! Let everyone living in the land tremble, for the day of the LORD is coming; it is near.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion; sound the alarm on my holy mountain. Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of the LORD is coming; indeed, it is near—

verses.rationale: Keeps dawn rather than silently making it darkness and preserves unparalleled scale.
verses.before: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness. Like dawn spread over the mountains, a great and mighty people comes. Nothing like it has been from ancient times, nor will there be again after it through the years of generation after generation.
verses.after: A day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness! Like dawn spreading over the mountains comes a vast and powerful people. Nothing like it has ever been, nor will be again for generations to come.
verses.tsw_comparator: a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and thick darkness. Like dawn spread over the mountains, a great and mighty people comes. Nothing like it has been from ancient times, nor will there be again after it through the years of generation after generation.

verses.rationale: Maintains before/behind pattern and Eden comparison.
verses.before: Before them fire devours, and behind them flame burns. The land before them is like the garden of Eden, but behind them a desolate wilderness, and nothing escapes them.
verses.after: Fire devours ahead of them; flame burns behind them. Before them the land is like the garden of Eden; behind them, a desolate wilderness. Nothing escapes them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before them fire devours, and behind them flame burns. The land before them is like the garden of Eden, but behind them a desolate wilderness, and nothing escapes them.

verses.rationale: Keeps comparisons rather than identifying the creatures as literal horsemen.
verses.before: Their appearance is like the appearance of horses, and like warhorses they run.
verses.after: They look like horses; they run like cavalry.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their appearance is like the appearance of horses, and like warhorses they run.

verses.rationale: Retains all three similes and the audible quality of the invasion.
verses.before: Like the sound of chariots they leap on the tops of the mountains, like the sound of a flame of fire devouring stubble, like a mighty people arranged for battle.
verses.after: With a sound like chariots they leap over the mountaintops, like the crackle of flame consuming stubble, like a powerful people drawn up for battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like the sound of chariots they leap on the tops of the mountains, like the sound of a flame of fire devouring stubble, like a mighty people arranged for battle.

verses.rationale: Chooses pallor for the uncertain facial expression while noting darkening as alternative.
verses.before: Before them peoples writhe; every face gathers pallor.
verses.after: Peoples writhe before them; every face loses its color.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before them peoples writhe; every face gathers pallor.

verses.rationale: Preserves ordered movement and the repeated military comparisons.
verses.before: They run like warriors; like men of war they climb the wall. Each goes in his own path, and they do not twist their ways.
verses.after: They run like warriors and scale a wall like soldiers. Each keeps to its own path; they do not swerve from their routes.
verses.tsw_comparator: They run like warriors; like men of war they climb the wall. Each goes in his own path, and they do not twist their ways.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult weapon phrase as penetration despite resistance, without asserting literal invulnerability.
verses.before: They do not press against one another; each goes on his own course. They plunge through the weapons and do not break formation.
verses.after: They do not jostle one another; each moves in its own lane. They plunge through the weapons and are not stopped.
verses.tsw_comparator: They do not press against one another; each goes on his own course. They plunge through the weapons and do not break formation.

verses.rationale: Preserves the four escalating locations and final thief simile.
verses.before: They rush upon the city; they run upon the wall. They climb into the houses; they enter through the windows like a thief.
verses.after: They rush upon the city, run along the wall, climb into the houses, and enter through the windows like a thief.
verses.tsw_comparator: They rush upon the city; they run upon the wall. They climb into the houses; they enter through the windows like a thief.

verses.rationale: Keeps cosmic response and literal celestial subjects rather than explaining an eclipse.
verses.before: Before them the earth trembles; the heavens shake. Sun and moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their brightness.
verses.after: Before them the earth shakes and the heavens tremble. Sun and moon grow dark; the stars withdraw their light.
verses.tsw_comparator: Before them the earth trembles; the heavens shake. Sun and moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their brightness.

verses.rationale: Maintains divine command, army, and the unanswered endurance question.
verses.before: The LORD gives his voice before his army, for his camp is very great; mighty is the one who carries out his word. For great is the day of the LORD and very awe-inspiring. Who can endure it?
verses.after: The LORD raises his voice before his army. His camp is vast; powerful is the one who carries out his word. The day of the LORD is great and deeply terrifying— who can endure it?
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD gives his voice before his army, for his camp is very great; mighty is the one who carries out his word. For great is the day of the LORD and very awe-inspiring. Who can endure it?

verses.rationale: Keeps even now as the interruption of judgment and the full threefold response.
verses.before: “Yet even now,” says the LORD, “return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with lamentation.”
verses.after: “Even now,” declares the LORD, “return to me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Yet even now,” says the LORD, “return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with lamentation.”

verses.rationale: Retains the bodily/clothing contrast and all attributes; disaster avoids confusing raah with moral evil here.
verses.before: Tear your hearts and not your garments. Return to the LORD your God, for he is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in steadfast love, and he relents concerning disaster.
verses.after: Tear your hearts, not your clothes, and return to the LORD your God. He is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and rich in faithful love, and he relents from bringing disaster.
verses.tsw_comparator: Tear your hearts and not your garments. Return to the LORD your God, for he is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in steadfast love, and he relents concerning disaster.

verses.rationale: Preserves uncertainty rather than turning repentance into a guaranteed outcome.
verses.before: Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave a blessing behind him— a grain offering and a drink offering for the LORD your God.
verses.after: Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave a blessing behind him— a grain offering and a drink offering for the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave a blessing behind him— a grain offering and a drink offering for the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Repeats the horn call and earlier assembly instructions exactly for recognition.
verses.before: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion; consecrate a fast; call a solemn assembly.
verses.after: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion! Set apart a fast; call a solemn assembly.
verses.tsw_comparator: Blow the ram’s horn in Zion; consecrate a fast; call a solemn assembly.

verses.rationale: Retains all ages and both newlyweds rather than only general everyone language.
verses.before: Gather the people; consecrate the congregation. Assemble the elders; gather the little children and those nursing at the breast. Let the bridegroom come out from his room and the bride from her canopy.
verses.after: Gather the people; set apart the congregation. Assemble the elders; gather children and nursing infants. Let the bridegroom leave his room and the bride her wedding chamber.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gather the people; consecrate the congregation. Assemble the elders; gather the little children and those nursing at the breast. Let the bridegroom come out from his room and the bride from her canopy.

verses.rationale: Follows rule-over sense of mashal while noting proverbial taunt alternative; preserves architectural location.
verses.before: Between the vestibule and the altar let the priests, the servants of the LORD, weep. Let them say: “Spare your people, O LORD, and do not make your inheritance a reproach, a byword among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, ‘Where is their God?’”
verses.after: Between the porch and the altar, let the priests who serve the LORD weep. Let them say, “Spare your people, LORD. Do not make your inheritance a disgrace, for nations to rule over them. Why should the peoples say, ‘Where is their God?’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Between the vestibule and the altar let the priests, the servants of the LORD, weep. Let them say: “Spare your people, O LORD, and do not make your inheritance a reproach, a byword among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, ‘Where is their God?’”

verses.rationale: Uses narrative past for the wayyiqtol turn without inventing an intervening repentance scene.
verses.before: Then the LORD became jealous for his land and had compassion on his people.
verses.after: Then the LORD became zealous for his land and had compassion on his people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD became jealous for his land and had compassion on his people.

verses.rationale: Keeps the restored three provisions and the reversal of public shame.
verses.before: The LORD answered and said to his people: “Look, I am sending you grain, new wine, and oil, and you will be satisfied by them. I will no longer make you a reproach among the nations.
verses.after: The LORD answered his people: “I am sending you grain, new wine, and oil, and you will have enough. I will no longer make you a disgrace among the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD answered and said to his people: “Look, I am sending you grain, new wine, and oil, and you will be satisfied by them. I will no longer make you a reproach among the nations.

verses.rationale: Leaves northern one unidentified and retains front/rear, two seas, and the ambiguous great deeds.
verses.before: I will remove the northern one far from you and drive it into a dry and desolate land, its front toward the eastern sea and its rear toward the western sea. Its stench will rise, and its foul smell will rise, for it has done great things.”
verses.after: I will drive the northern one far from you and thrust it into a dry, desolate land, its front into the eastern sea and its rear into the western sea. Its stench will rise, its foul smell will go up, for it has done great things.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will remove the northern one far from you and drive it into a dry and desolate land, its front toward the eastern sea and its rear toward the western sea. Its stench will rise, and its foul smell will rise, for it has done great things.”

verses.rationale: Repeats great things with a new subject and addresses the ground itself.
verses.before: Do not fear, O land; rejoice and be glad, for the LORD has done great things.
verses.after: Do not fear, ground! Celebrate and rejoice, for the LORD has done great things.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not fear, O land; rejoice and be glad, for the LORD has done great things.

verses.rationale: Keeps animals as direct addressees and reverses the earlier vegetation loss.
verses.before: Do not fear, animals of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness have become green. The tree bears its fruit; fig tree and vine give their strength.
verses.after: Do not fear, wild animals, for the wilderness pastures are green. The trees bear fruit; fig tree and vine give their full yield.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not fear, animals of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness have become green. The tree bears its fruit; fig tree and vine give their strength.

verses.rationale: Chooses rain in agricultural context, preserving righteousness and noting teacher and first-month alternatives.
verses.before: Children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the LORD your God, for he has given you the early rain for righteousness. He has poured down rain for you, the early rain and the later rain, as before.
verses.after: Children of Zion, celebrate and rejoice in the LORD your God. He has given you the autumn rain in righteousness; he sends rain down for you, autumn and spring rain as before.
verses.tsw_comparator: Children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the LORD your God, for he has given you the early rain for righteousness. He has poured down rain for you, the early rain and the later rain, as before.

verses.rationale: Keeps the produce and processing locations paired rather than generic abundance.
verses.before: The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
verses.after: The threshing floors will be full of grain; the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.

verses.rationale: Retains all four terms in this verse's different order and explicitly divine agency.
verses.before: “I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust ate, the hopping locust, the destroying locust, and the cutting locust— my great army that I sent among you.
verses.after: “I will repay you for the years eaten by the swarming locust, the creeping locust, the stripping locust, and the cutting locust— my great army that I sent against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust ate, the hopping locust, the destroying locust, and the cutting locust— my great army that I sent among you.

verses.rationale: Preserves satiation, praise, and the full no-shame promise.
verses.before: You will eat abundantly and be satisfied, and you will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has dealt wondrously with you. My people will never again be put to shame.
verses.after: You will eat your fill and praise the name of the LORD your God, who has done wonders for you. My people will never again be put to shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will eat abundantly and be satisfied, and you will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has dealt wondrously with you. My people will never again be put to shame.

verses.rationale: Repeats the promise unchanged and retains presence plus exclusivity.
verses.before: You will know that I am among Israel, that I am the LORD your God and there is no other. My people will never again be put to shame.
verses.after: You will know that I am among Israel, that I am the LORD your God and there is no other. My people will never again be put to shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will know that I am in the midst of Israel, that I am the LORD your God and there is no other. My people will never again be put to shame.

verses.rationale: Keeps all flesh, both sexes in prophecy, and age-specific dream/vision language.
verses.before: And afterward I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your elders will dream dreams; your young people will see visions.
verses.after: Afterward I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and daughters will prophesy; your old men will dream dreams; your young men will see visions.
verses.tsw_comparator: And afterward I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your elders will dream dreams; your young people will see visions.

verses.rationale: Makes enslavement explicit and preserves both sexes without adding my from a later quotation.
verses.before: Even upon male servants and female servants in those days I will pour out my Spirit.
verses.after: Even on male and female slaves I will pour out my Spirit in those days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even upon male servants and female servants in those days I will pour out my Spirit.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three signs without assigning a modern event.
verses.before: I will give wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.
verses.after: I will display wonders in the heavens and on earth: blood, fire, and columns of smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.

verses.rationale: Keeps the cosmic transformations and before relationship.
verses.before: The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and awe-inspiring day of the LORD comes.
verses.after: The sun will turn to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and terrifying day of the LORD comes.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and awe-inspiring day of the LORD comes.

verses.rationale: Preserves both human calling and divine calling and all three name occurrences.
verses.before: And it will be that everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape. For on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be people who escape, as the LORD has said, and among the survivors those whom the LORD calls.
verses.after: Everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape, for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the LORD has said, and among the survivors will be those the LORD calls.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it will be that everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will escape. For on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, as the LORD has said, and among the survivors those whom the LORD calls.

verses.rationale: Follows the read restore form and carries the temporal clause into the next verse.
verses.before: For look, in those days and at that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,
verses.after: “In those days and at that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, in those days and at that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

verses.rationale: Keeps the judgment setting, scattered people, and divided land as distinct charges.
verses.before: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. I will enter into judgment with them there concerning my people and my inheritance, Israel, whom they scattered among the nations, and they divided my land.
verses.after: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them for my people, my inheritance Israel, whom they scattered among the nations. They divided up my land.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. I will enter into judgment with them there concerning my people and my inheritance, Israel, whom they scattered among the nations, and they divided my land.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sex and age of the trafficked children and the explicit transactions.
verses.before: They cast lots for my people; they traded a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine and drank it.
verses.after: They cast lots for my people, traded a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine and drank it.
verses.tsw_comparator: They cast lots for my people; they traded a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine and drank it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated repayment root and named coastal regions.
verses.before: And what are you to me, Tyre and Sidon and all the regions of Philistia? Are you repaying me for something? If you are repaying me, swiftly and quickly I will return your repayment upon your own heads.
verses.after: And what have you against me, Tyre and Sidon and all the regions of Philistia? Are you repaying me for something? If you are paying me back, I will swiftly bring your repayment down on your own heads.
verses.tsw_comparator: And what are you to me, Tyre and Sidon and all the regions of Philistia? Are you repaying me for something? If you are repaying me, swiftly and quickly I will return your repayment upon your own heads.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine ownership and the destination, noting temple/palace range if needed.
verses.before: For you took my silver and my gold and carried my precious good things into your temples.
verses.after: You took my silver and gold and carried my finest treasures into your temples.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you took my silver and my gold and carried my precious good things into your temples.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named buyers and removal purpose without importing a conquest date.
verses.before: You sold the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem to the children of the Greeks in order to remove them far from their territory.
verses.after: You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks to send them far from their own territory.
verses.tsw_comparator: You sold the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem to the children of the Greeks in order to remove them far from their territory.

verses.rationale: Repeats the retribution clause and the victims' awakening from sale.
verses.before: Look, I am stirring them up from the place where you sold them, and I will return your repayment upon your own heads.
verses.after: Look, I will rouse them from the place where you sold them and bring your repayment down on your own heads.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am stirring them up from the place where you sold them, and I will return your repayment upon your own heads.

verses.rationale: Preserves the disturbing retaliatory enslavement and specific buyers without editorial endorsement.
verses.before: I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, to a nation far away, for the LORD has spoken.
verses.after: I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, a distant nation.” For the LORD has spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, to a nation far away, for the LORD has spoken.

verses.rationale: Retains consecration rather than merely preparation and the repeated mobilization.
verses.before: Proclaim this among the nations: Consecrate war! Stir up the warriors! Let all the men of war draw near; let them come up!
verses.after: Proclaim this among the nations: “Consecrate a war! Rouse the warriors! Let all the soldiers approach and advance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Proclaim this among the nations: Consecrate war! Stir up the warriors! Let all the men of war draw near; let them come up!

verses.rationale: Keeps the deliberate reversal of agricultural peace imagery and the weak fighter's boast.
verses.before: Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, “I am a warrior!”
verses.after: Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, ‘I am a warrior!’
verses.tsw_comparator: Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the weak say, “I am a warrior!”

verses.rationale: Marks the shift from nations' summons to prayer without merging the two armies.
verses.before: Hurry and come, all you surrounding nations; gather yourselves there. Bring down your warriors, O LORD!
verses.after: Hurry and come, all you surrounding nations; gather there!” Bring down your warriors, LORD!
verses.tsw_comparator: Hurry and come, all you surrounding nations; gather yourselves there. Bring down your warriors, O LORD!

verses.rationale: Preserves divine first-person judicial seating and repeated location.
verses.before: Let the nations stir themselves and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
verses.after: “Let the nations rouse themselves and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the nations stir themselves and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.

verses.rationale: Keeps harvest and vintage as judgment imagery with evil as explicit explanation.
verses.before: Put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread, for the winepress is full. The vats overflow, for their evil is great.
verses.after: Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread, for the winepress is full; the vats overflow, for their evil is great.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread, for the winepress is full. The vats overflow, for their evil is great.

verses.rationale: Repeats multitudes and valley; note clarifies divine verdict rather than an invitation to human decision.
verses.before: Multitudes, multitudes in the Valley of Decision! For the day of the LORD is near in the Valley of Decision.
verses.after: Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! The day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.
verses.tsw_comparator: Multitudes, multitudes in the Valley of Decision! For the day of the LORD is near in the Valley of Decision.

verses.rationale: Matches the recurring cosmic-darkness clause for literary recognition.
verses.before: Sun and moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their brightness.
verses.after: Sun and moon grow dark; the stars withdraw their light.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sun and moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their brightness.

verses.rationale: Keeps threatening roar alongside refuge and both divine-name occurrences.
verses.before: The LORD roars from Zion and gives his voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth shake. But the LORD is a refuge for his people and a stronghold for the children of Israel.
verses.after: The LORD roars from Zion and raises his voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth shake. But the LORD is a refuge for his people, a stronghold for the people of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD roars from Zion and gives his voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth shake. But the LORD is a refuge for his people and a stronghold for the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains strangers rather than silently restricting to invaders; explains hostile context in a note.
verses.before: Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, and strangers will pass through her no more.
verses.after: “You will know that I am the LORD your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, and strangers will no longer pass through her.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, dwelling in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, and strangers will pass through her no more.

verses.rationale: Preserves abundant liquids and the sanctuary spring without forcing a geographical identification.
verses.before: And on that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, and all the channels of Judah will flow with water. A spring will go out from the house of the LORD and water the Valley of Shittim.
verses.after: On that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, and all Judah’s streambeds will flow with water. A spring will flow from the house of the LORD and water the Valley of Acacias.
verses.tsw_comparator: And on that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, and all the channels of Judah will flow with water. A spring will go out from the house of the LORD and water the Valley of Shittim.

verses.rationale: Retains both nations and bloodshed as the reason, with possessive land ambiguity noted.
verses.before: Egypt will become a desolation, and Edom a desolate wilderness, because of violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.
verses.after: Egypt will become a desolation, and Edom a desolate wilderness, for violence against the people of Judah, whose innocent blood they shed in their land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Egypt will become a desolation, and Edom a desolate wilderness, because of violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

verses.rationale: Keeps enduring habitation distinct from a modern political application.
verses.before: Yet Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
verses.after: But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem through every generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned clear/acquit verb, noting vindicate/avenge readings and leaving the blood's referent cautious.
verses.before: I will hold innocent their blood that I had not held innocent, and the LORD dwells in Zion.
verses.after: I will clear their bloodguilt that I have not cleared.” The LORD dwells in Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will hold innocent their blood that I had not held innocent, and the LORD dwells in Zion.

comparative_references.scope: All 73 TSW verses bound and compared programmatically after independent drafting from each selected original-language record and all annotations. Selected differences read during focused authoring checks. Overlap is triage only.
